article_title: Fostering Early Numerical Skills at School Start in Children at Risk for Mathematical Achievement Problems: A Small Sample Size Training Study
citation: Marcus Hasselhorn & Kathrin Linke-Hasselhorn. (2013). Fostering Early Numerical Skills at School Start in Children at Risk for Mathematical Achievement Problems: A Small Sample Size Training Study. International Education Studies, 6(3). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/ies.v6n3p213
title: MZZ training program "Mengen, zählen, Zahlen" (Krajewski, Nieding, & Schneider, 2007)
description: MZZ is a German training program promoting early awareness of quantities, numbers and relations between numbers. The article describes it as one that "systematically builds up conceptual knowledge from practising basic skills to instruction in numerical structures" and "offers a clear structure of the numerical space, allowing for effective problem solving strategies". Children use graspable materials that represent the structure of numbers, so the abstract structure is rendered "tangible" and "visible". The program comprises three focal areas corresponding to competence levels I through III, delivered playfully in small groups; the manual specifies 24 sessions of 30 minutes.
requirements: The MZZ authors recommend application in small groups of up to six children to support particularly weak children at kindergarten
constraints: The article notes the program's evaluation suggests training should best be conducted shortly before school start to increase the probability of transfer to school achievement
target_learners: pre-school class children deferred from school entry with weak number competencies
examples: In this study the program was run in a separate room three times per week during regular lessons, in 24 sessions of 30 minutes with a playful atmosphere
